# Experimentation Health Scorecard
*Simulated program: 200 experiments, known ground truth. Generated by `experiment_autopsy`.*

| # | Check | Result | Status |
|---|-------|--------|--------|
| 1 | False positive rate under daily peeking | 23.0% (vs. nominal 5%) | 🔴 At risk |
| 1b | False positive rate, fixed-horizon (no peeking) | 5.3% | 🟢 Healthy |
| 1c | Exploratory mixture-test prototype (not validated as always-valid) | 1.5% | ⚠️ Exploratory; calibration incomplete |
| 2 | Minimum detectable relative lift at current traffic (14-day test, 16,800 users/arm) | 10.6% | — |
| 2b | Days needed to reliably detect a 5% relative lift | 62 days | 🔴 At risk |
| 3 | Experiments flagged for Sample Ratio Mismatch (p<0.01) | 8.5% of program | 🔴 At risk |
| 3b | SRM detection recall (of experiments we know are actually bugged) | 100.0% | 🟢 Healthy |
| 3c | Declared "winners" that were sitting on an undetected/undiagnosed SRM bug | 4 of 75 | 🔴 At risk |
| 4 | CUPED variance reduction (revenue-style metric, pre/post correlation 0.6) | 34.5% | 🟢 Adopt |
| 4b | Runtime reduction from CUPED, same %, applied to the 5%-lift test above | 62 days &rarr; 41 days | 🟢 Adopt |
| 5 | Novelty/decay effects present among true winners (simulated ground truth) | 31.6% | — |
| 5b | Novelty detection recall (time-slice interaction test) | 8.3% | 🔴 Underpowered |
| 5c | False novelty alarms on genuinely stable winners | 3.8% | 🟢 Low |
| 6 | False positive rate checking 5 metrics per test, no correction | 25.1% | 🔴 At risk |
| 6b | Same, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction | 5.2% | 🟢 Healthy |

## Headline
Out of 75 experiments declared "significant winners" under a
stop-when-significant policy, **26 (34.7%)
were false positives** (ground truth: no real effect). Running the identical 200
experiments under a disciplined fixed-horizon policy would have declared only
40 winners, of which 15.0% were false -
fewer false wins in absolute terms, at the cost of also missing some real ones that
peeking caught early (peeking isn't pure downside, it's a power/validity trade you're
currently making blind).

## Known limitations of this scorecard
- Ground truth is simulator-defined. Real programs don't get this, which is exactly why
  checks 1, 3, and 6 (process controls) matter more than any single p-value.
- Novelty detection recall (8.3%) is genuinely low here - not a bug,
  a finding. Detecting decay effects needs meaningfully more data than detecting the
  headline effect; don't expect a time-slice test to catch most novelty effects at
  typical 2-week experiment sample sizes.
- CUPED's payoff is metric-dependent. It was demonstrated here on a continuous,
  revenue-style metric with a realistic 0.6 pre/post correlation; a low-correlation or
  purely binary metric will see much less benefit (see memo).
